biodiversity_overview.text: 157,098 GBIF occurrence records for 106 tracked species are attributed to Maharashtra, spanning 1859-2026.
153,839 of these records (97.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 30, Magnoliopsida 21, Mammalia 16, Actinopterygii 13, Squamata 10, Testudines 7, Amphibia 5, Crocodylia 1, Cephalopoda 1, Arachnida 1, Liliopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 11 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Tiger (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Sloth Bear (VU), Asian Elephant (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Robin (12,449), Indian Grey-Hornbill (11,567), Indian Golden Oriole (10,977), White-throated Munia (10,907), Indian Spot-billed Duck (10,161).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 4,674 in 2016 to 1,739 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 2.93% of Maharashtra's area (55 areas intersect the state).
11.5% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (17,691 of 153,839); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Pellona (0.56), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Indian Scad (0.48).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Maharashtra (equal-weight reference): cell near 18.375N 73.875E (overall rank 2, median rank across weightings 7); cell near 21.375N 79.125E (overall rank 53, median rank across weightings 58); cell near 17.625N 73.125E (overall rank 57, median rank across weightings 82).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 10,882 km2 (3.57% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

227.4 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (2.09% of the 2000 extent; 0.79% in 2015-2024, rank 15 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2011 (21.35 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.14% of land and population density is 415.4 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
36% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
